trigger: A correct incumbent exists and one measured bottleneck is supported by evidence.
action: Keep the incumbent and change one bounded mechanism aimed at that bottleneck.
guardrails: Do not bundle unrelated structural changes; require a falsifiable expected signal.

trigger: The incumbent family is plausibly saturated or repeated local changes are flat.
action: Reset the architecture and propose a qualitatively different decomposition.
guardrails: Start from a frozen reference or explicit root; the child inherits no parent score.

trigger: At least two evidence-bearing attempts failed to improve and share an assumption.
action: State the shared assumption and construct a child that deliberately inverts it.
guardrails: The inverted assumption must be named; arbitrary novelty does not qualify.

trigger: Two frozen parents have complementary mechanisms or resource profiles.
action: Build a new child from explicit parent contributions and re-evaluate from zero.
guardrails: Do not splice arbitrary text; reject same-niche duplicates and inherited scores.

trigger: The latest attempt failed formatting, compilation, or correctness.
action: Repair the earliest failing contract before any performance optimization.
guardrails: A failed attempt remains in the denominator; environment errors are separate.

trigger: A new credible leader exposes a specific adjacent configuration to test.
action: Immediately allocate one bounded follow-up around the winning mechanism.
guardrails: The follow-up consumes the normal budget and may not inherit the leader score.

trigger: The recent window is stagnant and the archive contains more than one viable family.
action: Move budget away from exhausted local probes toward reset, inversion, or recombination.
guardrails: Use a frozen decision epoch and deterministic tie breaks.

trigger: Parent candidates cluster in one structural niche or the best score is unstable.
action: Select an elite or bridge from a different mechanically derived niche.
guardrails: Novelty is diagnostic only and cannot override correctness or the hard budget.

trigger: A proposal is high-risk or expensive and has not passed cheap checks.
action: Run format/static/correctness gates before full performance evaluation.
guardrails: A cheap proxy never mints a performance winner.

trigger: A sealed attempt has a reason-coded format, compile, correctness, or performance outcome.
action: Route the next proposal to the operator matching the earliest trustworthy failure stage.
guardrails: Environment-invalid outcomes are nondecisions; performance mutation cannot precede correctness.

trigger: More than one frozen parent is eligible and a high-scoring parent has already produced multiple children.
action: Balance parent quality with the number and outcomes of its existing children.
guardrails: Selection occurs on a sealed snapshot; a child never inherits parent fitness.

trigger: Evidence implicates coordination, information flow, or tool ordering rather than the final directive alone.
action: Mutate the typed role graph, step dependencies, or trusted component bindings.
guardrails: Generated executable plugins are forbidden; every graph node must resolve in the trusted registry.

trigger: The current decision has at least two sealed ancestors or a repeated failure signature.
action: First summarize full-archive patterns, then produce a parent-local falsifiable update.
guardrails: Reflection receives public typed records, never raw private logs or hidden tests.

trigger: A first-encounter instance trajectory is fully sealed and its score can no longer change.
action: Extract task descriptors, initial-Harness choices, update actions, outcomes, costs, counterexamples, and scope into versioned Experience Records before the next unseen instance.
guardrails: Never update the Builder before scoring the current instance; same-instance reruns become training diagnostics and cannot count as generalization.
